==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|promyse||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|promis|promis, promisse}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|promesse}}, from {{der|en|la-med|prōmissa}}, {{der|en|la|prōmissum|t=a promise}}, feminine and neuter past participles of {{m|la|prōmittō|t=to send forth, to say beforehand, to promise}}, from {{m|la|pro||forth}} + {{m|la|mittere||to send}}; see {{m|en|mission}}. Compare {{m|en|admit}}, {{m|en|commit}}, {{m|en|permit}}, etc. Displaced native {{m|ang|ġehātan||to promise}} and {{m|ang|ġehāt||a promise}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒmɪs/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑmɪs/|a=GA,Atlantic Canada}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-promise.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒmɪs/|a=CA,dialects of the US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɔmɪs/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|[ˈpɹɔ̟mɪs]|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒmɪs|q1=Received Pronunciation|ɑmɪs|q2=General American|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|prom|ise}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} An [[oath]] or [[affirmation]]; a [[vow]].
#: {{ux|en|When I make a '''promise''', I always stick to it.}}
#: {{ux|en|I asked him not to, and we all heard his '''promise''' that he wouldn't.}}
#: {{ux|en|He broke his '''promise''': he said he'd return my jewellery, but never did.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|legal}} A transaction between two persons whereby the first person undertakes in the future to render some service or gift to the second person or devotes something valuable now and here to their use.
# {{lb|en|countable}} Something promised.
#: {{ux|en|That jewelry was a '''promise''' to me.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Reason to expect improvement or success; [[potential]].
#: {{ux|en|His grade are poor, but I see '''promise''' in him.}}
#: {{ux|en|Your claim has little '''promise''' in court.}}
#: {{ux|en|She shows great '''promise''' as an actress.}}
#* {{RQ:Irving Sketch Book
|passage=My native country was full of youthful '''promise'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=1|passage=The original family who had begun to build a palace to rival Nonesuch had died out before they had put up little more than the gateway, so that the actual structure which had come down to posterity retained the secret magic of a '''promise''' rather than the overpowering splendour of a great architectural achievement.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Braving the Northwest Passage|author=Jeff MacInnis|page=586
|text=The dream of a Northwest Passage lured European explorers for centuries with the '''promise''' of a quick, if hazardous, Arctic sea route across the New World to the wealth of Asia.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|programming}} A [[placeholder]] [[object]] representing the eventual result of an [[asynchronous]] operation.
#* {{quote-web|en|date=August 25, 2023|publisher=Google|title=Observables compared to other techniques|work=Angular 17 documentation|url=https://v17.angular.io/guide/comparing-observables|text=You can often use observables instead of '''promises''' to deliver values asynchronously.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|obsolete}} [[bestowal|Bestowal]] or [[fulfillment]] of what is promised.
#: {{ux|en|It is time they receive their '''promise'''.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|1|4|passage=He {{...}} commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the '''promise''' of the Father.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{sid|en|to commit}} {{lb|en|ambitransitive|ditransitive}} To [[commit]] to (some action or outcome), or to [[assure]] (a person) of such commitment; to make an [[oath]] or [[vow]].
#* '''1936 Aug.''', {{w|Ernest Hemingway}}, "{{w|The Short Happy Life of Francis Macomber}}", ''{{w|Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan}}'':
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=70
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579879-buy-out-firm-really-does-focus-operational-improvements-engineers Engineers of a different kind]
|passage=Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers.{{...}}Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster. Clever financial ploys are what have made billionaires of the industry’s veterans. “Operational improvement” in a portfolio company has often meant little more than '''promising''' colossal bonuses to sitting chief executives if they meet ambitious growth targets. That model is still prevalent today.}}
#: {{ux|en|If you '''promise''' not to tell anyone, I will let you have this cake for free.}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''promised''' to never return to this town again.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''promised''' me a big kiss if I would drive him to the airport.}}
#: {{ux|en|I can't '''promise''' success, but I'll do the best I can.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To give grounds for [[expectation]], especially of something good.
#: {{ux|en|The clouds '''promise''' rain.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=I liked the man for his own sake, and even had he '''promised''' to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me. I look upon notoriety with the same indifference as on the buttons on a man's shirt-front, or the crest on his note-paper.}}

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the ''to infinitive''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]
